dist_transform_abs — 2D region op

• Data kinds: region → image

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "dist_transform_abs", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

• HALCON equivalent: distance_transform (the HALCON reference is a useful guide to its meaning and parameters)

*The figure is the actual output on a synthetic 128×128 input. Left: input, right: output. Point clouds are drawn as a top-down scatter (brightness = z), 1-D series as a line plot, volumes as the maximum-intensity projection along z, videos as the middle frame, complex images as magnitude; return values that are not pictures are shown as the values themselves.*

*The output is shown in a viridis-like pseudo-colour (dark purple = low, yellow = high) so that a field of quantities — distance, phase, orientation, depth — can be read.*

Usage

Distance transform in absolute pixel distances without normalisation. Equivalent to HALCON's distance_transform (Compute the distance transformation of a region.).

a selects the distance type: a < 1/3 Euclidean, 1/3 <= a < 2/3 city-block (L1), otherwise chessboard (L∞). b < 0.5 returns, for every foreground pixel, the distance to the nearest background pixel; b >= 0.5 returns, for every background pixel, the distance to the nearest foreground pixel. The output is a float64 image and, unlike dist_transform, is not normalised by the per-image maximum (the centres of a 3×3 and a 9×9 square are 2 and 5). Example: _dist_transform_abs(np.ones((3, 3)), 0, 0).

The HALCON reference operator returns int4 approximations. This op returns exact float64 distances and is not a compatibility API.

For a region containing NaN, NaN is treated as background during binarisation. With an all-background input plus one NaN and b >= 0.5, it returns -1 at every pixel, outside the image sort range.
